fields.name: sign
fields.text: The old gate creaks in the wind.

buttons.name: Ring the bell
buttons.sentence: Ring the bell and ask "Ding dong! Who's there?" with the choices A ghost or Nobody. If it's a ghost, a werewolf howls and the sign says "Something howled back."; otherwise the sign says "Nobody answered. Or did they?"
buttons.script:
on mouseUp
  answer "Ding dong! Who's there?" with "A ghost" or "Nobody"
  if it is "A ghost" then
    howl
    put "Something howled back." into field "sign"
  else
    put "Nobody answered. Or did they?" into field "sign"
  end if
end mouseUp

buttons.name: Open the gate

end mouseUp

  go to stack "Home"
end mouseUp

fields.name: greeting
fields.text: A candle flickers in the hall.

fields.name: note
fields.text: Something fluttered out of the closet!

buttons.name: Light a candle
buttons.sentence: Ask the visitor's name. With no name, write "The candle waits for a name." in greeting; otherwise write "Welcome, " and the name and a full stop there, and if the name contains Kiro, say "Oh! A friend of the house."
buttons.script:
on mouseUp
  ask "What is your name?"
  if it is empty then
    put "The candle waits for a name." into field "greeting"
  else
    put "Welcome, " & it & "." into field "greeting"
    if it contains "Kiro" then answer "Oh! A friend of the house."
  end if
end mouseUp

buttons.name: Open the closet
buttons.sentence: Let a bat out of the closet and show the note for two seconds.
buttons.script:
on mouseUp
  release bat
  show field "note"
  wait 2 seconds
  hide field "note"
end mouseUp

fields.name: body
fields.text:
Welcome to Stack Séance, HyperCard back from the dead.

Every button here grew from one plain sentence, apart from a couple broken on purpose for you to fix. Flip any card over and you see that sentence next to the script the spirits wrote for it. The script is what really runs, and you can change it.

buttons.name: Start the tour
buttons.sentence: Start the tour: open the next card with an iris.
buttons.script:
on mouseUp
  visual effect iris open
  go to next card
end mouseUp

buttons.name: Home
buttons.sentence: Go back to the Home stack.
buttons.script:
on mouseUp
  go to stack "Home"
end mouseUp

fields.name: body
fields.text:
Click a button to run its script. A button can take you to another card, ask you something, or let something out of the closet.

The Go menu at the top goes to the first, previous, next or last card of a stack, and Home. These buttons do the same:

buttons.name: First card
buttons.sentence: Go to the first card of this stack.
buttons.script:
on mouseUp
  go to first card
end mouseUp

buttons.name: Last card

buttons.script:

end mouseUp

fields.name: body
fields.text:
Every card has a back. Click the folded corner at the bottom right, or View › Flip, to turn it over.

The back shows each button's sentence and its HyperTalk script. Change a script and the button changes at once.

Try it: flip this card, change "Hello!" in Say hello, flip back and click it.

fields.name: body
fields.text:
Click + Button at the top right of the window, then click where the button should go. Write one sentence about what it should do, in any language, and click Grow.

The spirits turn your sentence into a script. A card it goes to that isn't there yet grows too. Whatever they can't do, a little ghost will tell you.

The button below grew from one sentence. Flip the card to read it.

fields.name: body
fields.text:
When a script goes wrong, a note pops up at the bottom of the card, naming the script and the line.

Click the note and the card flips over to that line, lit up, so you can see what went wrong and fix it.

This button is broken on purpose. Click it, then click the note.

fields.name: body
fields.text:
File › Saves keeps three copies of every stack in this browser. Export a save to a file to keep it or take it to another computer, and import it back.

File › Settings: day or night, pixel or plain font, bigger text on the back of the card, and Revert to original for when a script is broken beyond repair.
